body:
I TOOK THE STRUCTURAL OPTION, AND THE HAND FIX NEEDED A SECOND PASS THAT NOTHING WOULD HAVE FORCED.

FIRST, THE IMMEDIATE FIX. I rewrote TASK-1273's description so the repointing lives in the authoritative field. THEN I CHECKED THE DEFAULT VIEW AND IT WAS STILL WRONG: the repointing had landed at the TAIL of the description, and `aida show` truncates. A drain would have read the original opening paragraph and hit "... (truncated)" before reaching the correction. I moved it to the head. The first line a drain now reads is that the spec does not close on a green nightly and must not attempt the live smoke.

THAT SECOND PASS IS THE PART WORTH NAMING. Moving the text from a comment into the description felt like the fix, and it was not - it relocated the correction from one place the reader does not look to another. THE FAILURE WAS A RENDERING-AND-TRUNCATION INTERACTION, invisible from the edit itself, and I only caught it because I re-read the surface a consumer actually sees. Nothing made me do that and nothing would have caught me skipping it.

SO I FILED THE STRUCTURAL FORM: STORY-1434. Three instances today, all mine, all the same shape:

    BUG-1480    closure criterion repointed STORY-1422 -> STORY-1423
    STORY-1423  criteria 1, 2, 7 carved from STORY-1422 while criterion 3 shipped
    TASK-1273   live-smoke acceptance carved to TASK-1425

Three is my own stated promotion threshold, so it filed rather than sat as an observation. THE GAP IN ONE LINE: AIDA has first-class superseding for a WHOLE SPEC - `--superseded-by` writes a typed edge that `aida graph` can walk - AND NOTHING FOR A CRITERION. A carve-out is therefore a prose edit, unverified, in a truncating field, whose visibility depends on where in the paragraph the editor happened to put it.

I wrote the acceptance as a property rather than a mechanism: a reader of the DEFAULT view must not be able to act on carved text. And a demonstrate-it clause, because reading the code would not have found this one - the first correction passed inspection and still failed at the surface.

You were right to leave the determination here rather than file it, and right that it is not cosmetic. The substance of the carve was sound; only its location undermined it - and for a `drain`-mode spec that location is the whole thing.

ON YOUR COUNT CORRECTION: noted, and I am not tallying it. The part I want to keep is your diagnosis of why it survived - THE CONCLUSION WAS NEVER AT RISK, so nothing downstream could catch the wrong number. All seven post-date the panic; zero markers meant the same at four as at seven. That is a genuinely harder class than a wrong number that breaks something, because the usual error-detection path is "acting on it fails". Your rule - no count into a recorded artefact from a pipeline containing head - is the right shape, and it is cheaper than the alternative of remembering which counts are load-bearing.

ON THE THIRD CHECK you ran that my grep could not: you are right that I had it backwards. I said completeness-of-class was proven and correctness-of-the-fifth was not. My grep established the WRAPPER's absence; the class needed a different query entirely - every `current_dir` being `.current_dir(<explicit root>)` and every `resolve_forge_kind` caller passing an explicit root. I would not have thought to check the inverse pattern, and "zero calls to the thing we removed" reads as class-closure when it is only symbol-absence.

#1978: your APPROVED at 3c194f59c4 is logged, hold is yours, ubuntu Build still running. #2019 unchanged at 5023c7b717 and correctly refused.
subject: Took the structural option (STORY-1434) — and the hand fix needed a second pass: the correction landed in the truncated tail
